title: Serre's criterion for affineness
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme. Assume that $X$ is quasi-compact, that $X$ is
quasi-separated, and that $\mathrm H^1(X,\mathcal I)=0$ for every
quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals $\mathcal I\subset\mathcal O_X$ of
finite type. Then $X$ is affine.
(*Stacks Project, Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 30.3.2, Tag
[01XG](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01XG).*)

proof.text: Let $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ be a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals. Since $X$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, by [lemma-nagata-ideal-directed-union-finite-type] (first paragraph; Properties, Tag 01PG) the quasi-coherent subideals $\mathcal K\subseteq\mathcal I$ of finite type form a family directed under inclusion whose union is $\mathcal I$; with the inclusions as transition maps, $\mathcal I$ together with the inclusions $\mathcal K\hookrightarrow\mathcal I$ is therefore a colimit of this directed system in the category of $\mathcal O_X$-modules (a directed union of subsheaves is their colimit). The hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-qs-scheme-cohomology-directed-colimit] hold for $X$: the affine opens, which are quasi-compact, form a basis of the topology, and the intersection of two quasi-compact opens is a finite union of intersections of two affine opens, hence quasi-compact by quasi-separatedness. Applying it with $U=X$ and $q=1$, every class in $H^1(X,\mathcal I)$ comes from some $H^1(X,\mathcal K)$ with $\mathcal K$ of finite type, which is zero by hypothesis. Hence $H^1(X,\mathcal I)=0$ for every quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals $\mathcal I$.

proof.text: The hypotheses of the quasi-compact vanishing criterion (Tag 01XF) now hold: $X$ is quasi-compact by assumption and $H^1(X,\mathcal I)=0$ for every quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals by step 1. Therefore $X$ is affine.
